parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, facility ban, custody rule or documented police/border targeting of trans visitors is recorded, and courts decriminalised same-sex conduct in 2024, protected health-care impartiality is documented, and LGBT assembly/pride proceeded without impediment. That documented acceptance places this above thin-protection jurisdictions. It sits a step below the acceptance-plus-working-protections tier because sexual-conduct law remains on the books, the 2024 decriminalisation is under appeal with contested implementation, there is no explicit gender-identity anti-discrimination law, organised political hostility and a December 2024 legislative override of foreign same-sex marriage recognition create partner/residency exposure, and traveller-facing remedies are undocumented.

entry_documents.exposure: Same-sex partner residency non-recognition: 2023 ruling confined by officials to case couples, litigant issued visitor visa on exit, and December 2024 act forbids recognition of foreign same-sex marriages. No general border trans-targeting documented.
entry_documents.protection: 2023 highest-court ruling required recognition of foreign same-sex marriages for immigration; 2024 courts recognised same-sex partners' residency rights per UN review, though implementation contested.
entry_documents.interaction: A trans visitor whose relationship is read as same-sex may be treated as visitor rather than spouse, affecting partner travel/residency; override interacts with unresolved appeal to weaken reliance on court rulings.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Historic sodomy offence remains on statute book, government said no intention to repeal; public affection between two men may be treated as immoral under 1980 act. Historic offence not believed used since 1990 (dated).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: High court declared sodomy/unnatural offences references in immigration act unconstitutional 21 June 2024; December 2024 UN review records courts decriminalised same-sex conduct in 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Unresolved July 2024 government appeal leaves current enforceability uncertain; this is secondary sexuality law, with no documented use against gender-nonconforming visitors in dossier.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward, shelter, custody-placement or facility-access rule for trans visitors is stated.

care_services.exposure: 2009 psychology scope regulations treat sexual and gender identity as disorders (dated, status in practice unclear). No documented visitor care denial.
care_services.protection: 2010 health professions ethical guidelines prohibit discrimination including sexual orientation and require beliefs not prejudice care; ministry patient charter requires impartial equal treatment irrespective of sex, gender and sexuality.
care_services.interaction: Health anti-discrimination protections are documented but dated/narrow and not shown to be enforced for visitors; ministerial charter mitigates but does not eliminate the older disorder classification.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Organised political hostility: 2014 anti-gay party launch, governing youth league listed opposing LGBTQ rights, hostile parliamentary marriage bills amplifying non-implementation of rulings.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Broadcasting code (2018) bars incitement to hatred based on gender or sexual orientation; courts issued pro-equality decriminalisation and residency rulings in 2023-2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State institutions are not documented as targeting trans people, but legislature and officials resist court rulings, weakening the protective value of formal rulings for travellers.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No rule on travelling trans minors, guardians, schooling or care access for minors is stated.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence, police harassment or extortion documented. Organised political hostility is documented, but no pattern of street attacks on visitors.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Pride marches 2013, 2017, 2018 (hundreds, two cities) and lesbian festival proceeded without government impediment; first LGBT drop-in centre opened 2018, indicating tolerated public presence (dated evidence).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Tolerance is concentrated in capital and coastal town; conditions elsewhere are expectation only, not documented, so protection may not extrapolate nationally.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Constitutional equality provision omits gender identity/sexual orientation; UN 2016 recommendation to legislate against discrimination not shown adopted; implementation of 2023-2024 rulings contested; July 2024 appeal outcome unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have provided relief in individual cases (2018 interim entry, 2023 marriage recognition, 2024 decriminalisation), showing some judicial recourse exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Individualised orders and legislative override mean remedies do not reliably generalise to a short-stay visitor, especially for partner status; unknowns are open questions, not documented traveller detention.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that courts/rules are formally protective but frontline/administrative implementation is uneven and remedies require advocacy; here no brief detention is documented and decriminalisation is recent, but legislative non-compliance is more systemic, so rating is close to 0.65.

Lower than 0.75-C because that anchor has explicit document recognition, training, tribunal appeal and compensation for unlawful detention; here gender-identity discrimination law is absent, the 2024 appeal is unresolved, and partner recognition was legislatively overridden.

Materially below 0.85-A: that anchor has explicit national equality law covering gender identity, independent oversight and documented disciplinary/compensation outcomes; here no such explicit GI protection or enforcement record is documented, and organised hostility persists.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: courts and health/broadcasting rules supply partial, documented protection and LGBT public life is tolerated, with no documented trans-specific targeting, facility exclusion or custody exposure. Countervailing exposures are secondary but real: residual sodomy/immorality law under unresolved appeal, no explicit GI anti-discrimination statute, organised political hostility, and legislative/administrative refusal to generalise partner-recognition rulings. For an adult alone, outing most plausibly risks friction, discrimination or partner-status problems rather than imprisonment; for minors/guardians no operative rule is documented. Interaction of hostile legislature with pro-equality courts leaves protection paper-thin in practice, supporting a score in the upper Elevated/Reduced boundary.
